Fix a constitution $c$ with $C\ge1$ named species and its equilibrium state domain $D_c\subseteq\mathbb R^{C+2}$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. An interior composition is represented by

$$
x=(x_1,\ldots,x_{C-1})\in\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}:=\{x\in\mathbb R^{C-1}:x_i>0,\ \sum_{i=1}^{C-1}x_i<1\},
$$

with $x_C:=1-\sum_{i<C}x_i>0$; for $C=1$, $\mathbb R^0=\{0\}$ and $x_1=1$.

A **phase branch** $\alpha$ is model data consisting of an open chart $W_\alpha\subseteq(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\times\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}\times(0,\infty)$ with coordinates $(T,p,x,m)$ and a $C^1$ diffeomorphism $\sigma_\alpha:W_\alpha\to U_\alpha$ onto an open subset $U_\alpha\subseteq\mathbb R^{C+2}$ contained in the equilibrium state domain $D_c$. Here $T$ is in kelvins, $p$ is in pascals, $m$ is total amount in moles, and $C^1$ means continuous first coordinate derivatives as in [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. The chart dimension is $C+2$, matching the ambient dimension of $D_c$. The map $\sigma_\alpha$ takes values in numerical state coordinates; its physical SI state map is explicitly $\chi_\alpha=\Phi_c\circ\sigma_\alpha$, where $\Phi_c$ is the numerical-to-SI unit map of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. Thus the physical amounts at this point are $n_j=m x_j$, and the numerical amount coordinates in $\sigma_\alpha$ are $n_j/(1\,\mathrm{mol})$. Derivative-defined physical state functions are evaluated on $\chi_\alpha(T,p,x,m)$, or equivalently pulled back along $\Phi_c$ to $\sigma_\alpha(T,p,x,m)$. At $\sigma_\alpha(T,p,x,m)$ in this precise pullback sense, the derivative-defined state functions of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]] give temperature $T$, pressure $p$, and mole fractions $x_j=n_j/m$; here $n_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\sum_{i=1}^C n_i=m$ uses the finite-sum convention of [[def-finite-sum]]. An **intensive phase branch** additionally has each derivative-defined chemical potential $\mu_j(T,p,x,m)$ independent of $m$ throughout $W_\alpha$; write its value as $\mu_j^\alpha(T,p,x)$. This scale invariance is an explicit constitutive model property, not a consequence of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]]. A valid local response chart and its inverse are as in [[def-td-response-functions]] and [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]. Existence of $W_\alpha$ or $\sigma_\alpha$ is a model premise, not a consequence of the equations of thermodynamics.

On a branch with a valid natural-variable chart, $G^\alpha$ denotes the Gibbs potential of [[def-td-legendre-potentials]] restricted to the branch. For a one-component branch with amount $m_\alpha>0$, define $g_\alpha:=G^\alpha/m_\alpha$, $s_\alpha:=S_\alpha/m_\alpha$, and $v_\alpha:=V_\alpha/m_\alpha$, in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, respectively. These quotients need not be independent of amount, and $g_\alpha=\mu^\alpha$ is not assumed by this definition. Such an equality requires a separate same-tag homogeneity hypothesis on the branch.

A **phase mixture** of a finite list of branches is a feasible separated compound whose positive phase amounts $m_\alpha$ have fractions $\lambda_\alpha:=m_\alpha/\sum_\beta m_\beta>0$ with $\sum_\alpha\lambda_\alpha=1$. Its extensive coordinates and entropy are those supplied by [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] and [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]], on the exact feasible set of [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The mixture is in **coexistence** when it is an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint under the declared totals and permitted exchanges, as in [[post-td-entropy-maximum]]. This definition does not assert that a maximum exists, that all branches can exchange every coordinate, or that metastable states are global equilibria.

The bulk scaling postulate may send a material tag $c$ to a different tag $c^{(\lambda)}$. It therefore does not supply same-tag degree-one homogeneity of $G^\alpha$ or $U^\alpha$ on a phase branch. Any result using $g_\alpha=\mu^\alpha$ must state that additional hypothesis.

Let $\mathcal F$ be the explicitly declared feasible endpoint set of an isolated compound whose constituents are independent separated macroscopic systems, as defined in [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. For this route, adopt the physical criterion that any endpoint tuple the model classifies as a stable equilibrium under these fixed totals, retained partitions, and permitted exchanges satisfies

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^{\mathrm{eq}})=\max_{x\in\mathcal F}S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x),\qquad S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x):=\sum_{i=1}^{m}S_{c_i}(x_i),$$

Here $\max$ means that $x^{\mathrm{eq}}\in\mathcal F$ and $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^{\mathrm{eq}})\ge S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x)$ for every $x\in\mathcal F$, using maximum in the sense of [[def-max-min]]. The finite sum is as in [[def-finite-sum]], and the summands are those of the separated macroscopic constituents under [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Whenever the stable-equilibrium label is used, attainment is assumed: at least one maximizing endpoint lies in $\mathcal F$. If $\mathcal F$ is empty or the entropy supremum is not attained, this item supplies no equilibrium state.

“Global” refers to every endpoint in this exact $\mathcal F$, not just nearby states, states reachable by a restricted short-time dynamics, or states on a selected branch. A local maximum that is not global, or a long-lived preparation trapped by kinetic barriers, is not declared stable equilibrium by this postulate. No uniqueness or relaxation dynamics is assumed.

Let $A$ and $B$ be two named subsystems with disjoint physical regions as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]], combined as a compound system $A\sqcup B$ inside a declared outer boundary. The model's admitted separated pairs form a specified subset $\mathcal C_{AB}\subseteq D_A\times D_B$ using [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]] and [[def-cartesian-product]]. For every pair $(x_A,x_B)\in\mathcal C_{AB}$, the composition map $\kappa_{AB}:\mathcal C_{AB}\to D_{A\sqcup B}$ is a function ([[def-function-space]]) adopted so the dimensioned coordinates of its output satisfy
$$U_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=U_A(x_A)+U_B(x_B),\qquad V_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=V_A(x_A)+V_B(x_B),\qquad n_{A\sqcup B,j}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=n_{A,j}(x_A)+n_{B,j}(x_B).$$
Here each coordinate function is the dimensioned map of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]] for its material constitution, with SI units as in [[def-td-si-quantities]].

Here “extensive coordinates” means precisely the named coordinates declared additive by this postulate. Amount coordinates are aligned by species label; when a species is absent from one subsystem, its zero amount is in a separately declared composition boundary, not the positive-mole chart of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. This is an idealized composition rule: cross-interface and long-range interaction energy is omitted from $U_{A\sqcup B}$, rather than asserted to vanish in nature. The postulate does not assert that every pair of subsystem states is physically admissible.

The framework's bulk family is a tagged family of material types. For each dimensionless scale $\lambda>0$ the model may designate a tag $c^{(\lambda)}$ and a subset $B_{c,\lambda}\subseteq D_c$ of states admitting a scaled copy, with inclusion as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in B_{c,\lambda}$, the scaling map is the function $\delta_\lambda:B_{c,\lambda}\to D_{c^{(\lambda)}}$ ([[def-function-space]]) given by $\delta_\lambda(x)=(\lambda\hat U,\lambda\hat V,\lambda\hat n_1,\ldots,\lambda\hat n_r)$. The tag matters: $c^{(\lambda)}$ is not silently identified with $c$. This postulate specifies the coordinate scaling model and energy additivity only; it does not postulate entropy additivity or exact scaling for every finite physical body.

This is an adopted physical composition rule, not a deduction from SI units or from the mathematics of Cartesian products.

Fix a material constitution $c$ and its equilibrium state domain $D_c$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. Let $\Omega\subseteq D_c$ be a specified open, single-phase chart in physical SI coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, with $U$ evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame of [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]]. On $\Omega$, use the finite $C^2$ entropy function $S_c$ and the strict positivity $S_{c,U}>0$ adopted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Here $C^2$ means that all coordinate partial derivatives through order two exist and are continuous ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). A coordinate partial such as $S_{c,U}$ is the ordinary derivative in that coordinate direction while every other physical coordinate is held fixed, as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

Define the **absolute thermodynamic temperature**, **entropic pressure**, and **molar chemical potential** of species $j$ by

$$T_c:=\frac{1}{S_{c,U}},\qquad p_c:=T_cS_{c,V},\qquad \mu_{c,j}:=-T_cS_{c,n_j}.$$

The entropy unit is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, the energy $U$ is in joules, $V$ is in cubic metres, and $n_j$ is in moles ([[def-td-si-quantities]]). Thus $S_{c,U}$ has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$, $T_c$ is finite and positive in kelvins, $S_{c,V}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$ and $p_c$ has units pascals, and $S_{c,n_j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ and $\mu_{c,j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$. If a microscopic model instead uses a dimensionless particle count $N_j=N_{\!A}n_j$, the corresponding per-particle chemical potential is $\mu_{c,j}/N_{\!A}$ joules, with the exact SI Avogadro constant from [[def-td-si-quantities]].

These are scalar state functions of the stated rest-frame equilibrium chart. The pressure in this definition is a derivative-defined conjugate; identifying it with force per area requires a separate adopted mechanical coupling. Neither an empirical thermometer calibration nor any equation of state is supplied by this definition.

Let $C\ge1$ be the number of components and $P\ge1$ the number of phases. Use common positive real coordinates $T,p$, expressed in fixed units if they are given a physical interpretation, and, for each phase $\alpha$, an interior composition vector

$$x^\alpha\in\Omega_C:=\{x\in\mathbb R^{C-1}:x_i>0,\ \sum_{i=1}^{C-1}x_i<1\},$$

with the convention $\mathbb R^0=\{0\}$ and $\Omega_1=\{0\}$. The final component fraction is $1-\sum_{i<C}x_i>0$. The ambient coordinate domain $U=(0,\infty)^2\times\Omega_C^P$ is open in $\mathbb R^n$, where $n=2+P(C-1)$. For each phase $\alpha$ and component $i$, let $\mu_i^\alpha(T,p,x^\alpha)$ be a real-valued $C^1$ coordinate function; these are mathematical maps and no thermodynamic potential or physical realization is assumed.

For $P\ge2$, define the $q=C(P-1)$ coexistence equations

$$F_{i,\alpha}(T,p,x^1,\ldots,x^P)=\mu_i^\alpha(T,p,x^\alpha)-\mu_i^1(T,p,x^1)=0\quad(1\le i\le C,\ 2\le\alpha\le P).$$

At a solution $z_*\in U$, assume some $q\times q$ derivative minor of $F:U\to\mathbb R^q$ is invertible. Then the local solution set is a graph of dimension

$$n-q=2+P(C-1)-C(P-1)=C-P+2.$$

For $P=1$ there are no coexistence equations and the coordinate domain itself has dimension $n=C+1=C-P+2$. In a specified reactive variant with $R\ge1$, let $\nu^1,\ldots,\nu^R\in\mathbb R^C$ be linearly independent dimensionless stoichiometric vectors and add the $R$ affinity equations $A_r=\sum_{i=1}^C\nu_i^r\mu_i^1=0$. If the combined equation map has an invertible $(q+R)\times(q+R)$ derivative minor at a solution and $q+R\le n$, its local zero set has dimension

$$n-q-R=C-P+2-R.$$

These are conditional local dimensions under the displayed nonsingular-minor assumptions. No dimension formula follows at singular solutions, on composition boundaries, or from equation counting alone; no empirical or general physical phase rule is asserted.

Let $1\le q\le n$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^q$ be $C^1$ in the sense of [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]. Suppose $F(x_*)=0$ and some $q\times q$ minor of the derivative matrix $DF(x_*)$ is invertible. This nonsingular-minor hypothesis is the explicit full-row-rank condition used here. If $q<n$, then after permuting coordinates $x=(u,v)\in\mathbb R^{n-q}\times\mathbb R^q$, there are open neighborhoods $P$ of $u_*$ and $Q$ of $v_*$ and a unique $C^1$ map $\varphi:P\to Q$ such that

$$F(u,v)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v=\varphi(u)\qquad((u,v)\in P\times Q).$$

Its derivative is

$$D\varphi(u)=-D_vF(u,\varphi(u))^{-1}D_uF(u,\varphi(u)).$$

Thus the local zero set is a graph over $n-q$ free coordinates. If $q=n$, the zero is locally isolated, so the local graph dimension is zero. Here “local graph dimension $k$” means a local graph parameterized by an open subset of $\mathbb R^k$, with a singleton counted as dimension zero.

derivations.claim: For $P\ge2$, define the phase-equality components $F_{i,\alpha}:=\mu_i^\alpha-\mu_i^1$ for $1\le i\le C$, $2\le\alpha\le P$. There are exactly $q=C(P-1)$ such scalar equations. By [A1], each $\mu_i^\alpha$ is C1 on the common open domain, so their finite differences are C1. By [F1], these equations hold at the stated physical coexistence point when the corresponding species exchanges are admitted; [A2] supplies the entropy regularity and positive temperatures required by that supplier.

Fix any phase $\alpha$ and reaction direction $
u^r$. Vary only that phase's species amounts as $n^\alpha(t)=n^{\alpha,*}+t
u^r$, holding its energy and volume and all other phase coordinates fixed; $t$ is a small extent in moles. By the stated bilateral feasibility, this curve is admitted for both signs of sufficiently small $t$. The total entropy has a local maximum at $t=0$ by [F2]. Its differentiability there follows from [A2]. The right difference quotients are nonpositive and the left difference quotients are nonnegative; the derivative is therefore zero. Additivity and [F3] give
$$
0= rac{dS_{\mathrm{tot}}}{dt}(0)=\sum_j S_{\alpha,n_j}
u_j^r=- rac{(
u^r)^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha}{T}.
$$
Since $T>0$, $(
u^r)^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha=0$ in every phase. The equations are C1 because they are finite linear combinations of the C1 branch maps. By [F1], phase equalities make the affinity equation identical across phases, so count only the $R$ equations in phase 1. The combined map therefore has $q+R$ equations.

The ambient coordinate dimension is $n=2+P(C-1)$. If $q+R=0$, then $P=1$ and $R=0$, so there are no phase-equality or reaction-affinity equations. The local zero set is all of the open chart and has dimension $n=2+(C-1)=C-P+2-R$.

If $q+R\ge1$, apply [L1] on the stated open chart $\mathcal U=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\times(\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ})^P$ to the combined C1 equation map using the stated invertible minor. The local graph theorem applies on this full chart, including all real pressures in the statement. Its local zero set has dimension
$$
n-q-R=2+P(C-1)-C(P-1)-R=C-P+2-R.
$$
This conclusion is conditional on the full-rank minor; it does not follow from equation counting alone. Additional stability constraints may reduce the physical coexistence set.

Assume the entropy of each phase is $C^2$ on its physical state chart and its derivative-defined temperature at the endpoint is finite and positive. The equation-set dimension below concerns this smooth interior state only.

Let $C\ge1$ be the number of named species, $P\ge1$ the number of coexisting phase branches, and $R\ge0$ the number of independent internal reaction directions. Consider an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint on the exact feasible set of [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. For each phase $\alpha$, use an intensive phase branch from [[def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain]] and an interior composition $x^\alpha\in\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}$. Let each branch chemical-potential map
$$
\mu^\alpha(T,p,x^\alpha)=(\mu_1^\alpha,\ldots,\mu_C^\alpha)
$$
be $C^1$ on a common open domain
$$
\mathcal U=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\times(\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ})^P \subseteq\mathbb R^{\,n},\qquad n=2+P(C-1).
$$
Assume energy, volume, and every named species can be exchanged between every phase pair in both directions, and every listed reaction direction is feasible in both extent directions in every phase while that phase's energy, volume, other reaction extents, and all other phase coordinates are held fixed at the coexistence point. Let $\nu^1,\ldots,\nu^R\in\mathbb R^C$ be linearly independent, dimensionless stoichiometric vectors, with extents measured in moles. Phase equilibrium imposes $\mu_i^\alpha-\mu_i^1=0$ for $1\le i\le C$, $2\le\alpha\le P$; internal reaction equilibrium imposes $(\nu^r)^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha=0$ in every phase for $1\le r\le R$. On the phase-equality locus these are the same $R$ equations in each phase, so count them once using phase 1. Put $q:=C(P-1)$ and $m:=q+R$. If $m=0$ (equivalently $P=1,R=0$), no equation is imposed and the local zero set is the whole chart, of dimension $n=C+1=C-P+2-R$. If $m\ge1$ and the combined equation map has an invertible $m\times m$ derivative minor at the solution, with $m\le n$, then the local zero set of these first-order coexistence-and-affinity equations is a graph of dimension
$$
n-q-R=C-P+2-R.
$$
This is the dimension of the equation zero set in intensive coordinates only; phase amounts and their extensive conservation constraints are not counted, and the actual stable-coexistence set may be a proper subset after additional stability constraints. If the nonsingular-minor condition fails, no dimension formula is asserted.

Fix a constitution $c$ with $C\ge1$ named species and its equilibrium state domain $D_c\subseteq\mathbb R^{C+2}$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. An interior composition is represented by

$$
x=(x_1,\ldots,x_{C-1})\in\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}:=\{x\in\mathbb R^{C-1}:x_i>0,\ \sum_{i=1}^{C-1}x_i<1\},
$$

with $x_C:=1-\sum_{i<C}x_i>0$; for $C=1$, $\mathbb R^0=\{0\}$ and $x_1=1$.

A **phase branch** $\alpha$ is model data consisting of an open chart $W_\alpha\subseteq(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\times\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}\times(0,\infty)$ with coordinates $(T,p,x,m)$ and a $C^1$ diffeomorphism $\sigma_\alpha:W_\alpha\to U_\alpha$ onto an open subset $U_\alpha\subseteq\mathbb R^{C+2}$ contained in the equilibrium state domain $D_c$. Here $T$ is in kelvins, $p$ is in pascals, $m$ is total amount in moles, and $C^1$ means continuous first coordinate derivatives as in [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. The chart dimension is $C+2$, matching the ambient dimension of $D_c$. At $\sigma_\alpha(T,p,x,m)$, the derivative-defined state functions of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]] give temperature $T$, pressure $p$, and mole fractions $x_j=n_j/m$; here $n_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\sum_{i=1}^C n_i=m$ uses the finite-sum convention of [[def-finite-sum]]. An **intensive phase branch** additionally has each derivative-defined chemical potential $\mu_j(T,p,x,m)$ independent of $m$ throughout $W_\alpha$; write its value as $\mu_j^\alpha(T,p,x)$. This scale invariance is an explicit constitutive model property, not a consequence of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]]. A valid local response chart and its inverse are as in [[def-td-response-functions]] and [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]. Existence of $W_\alpha$ or $\sigma_\alpha$ is a model premise, not a consequence of the equations of thermodynamics.

On a branch with a valid natural-variable chart, $G^\alpha$ denotes the Gibbs potential of [[def-td-legendre-potentials]] restricted to the branch. For a one-component branch with amount $m_\alpha>0$, define $g_\alpha:=G^\alpha/m_\alpha$, $s_\alpha:=S_\alpha/m_\alpha$, and $v_\alpha:=V_\alpha/m_\alpha$, in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, respectively. These quotients need not be independent of amount, and $g_\alpha=\mu^\alpha$ is not assumed by this definition. Such an equality requires a separate same-tag homogeneity hypothesis on the branch.

A **phase mixture** of a finite list of branches is a feasible separated compound whose positive phase amounts $m_\alpha$ have fractions $\lambda_\alpha:=m_\alpha/\sum_\beta m_\beta>0$ with $\sum_\alpha\lambda_\alpha=1$. Its extensive coordinates and entropy are those supplied by [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] and [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]], on the exact feasible set of [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The mixture is in **coexistence** when it is an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint under the declared totals and permitted exchanges, as in [[post-td-entropy-maximum]]. This definition does not assert that a maximum exists, that all branches can exchange every coordinate, or that metastable states are global equilibria.

The bulk scaling postulate may send a material tag $c$ to a different tag $c^{(\lambda)}$. It therefore does not supply same-tag degree-one homogeneity of $G^\alpha$ or $U^\alpha$ on a phase branch. Any result using $g_\alpha=\mu^\alpha$ must state that additional hypothesis.

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^{\mathrm{eq}})=\max_{x\in\mathcal F}S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x),\qquad S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x):=\sum_{i=1}^{m}S_{c_i}(x_i),$$

On $\Omega$, use the finite $C^2$ entropy function $S_c$ and the strict positivity $S_{c,U}>0$ adopted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Here $C^2$ means that all coordinate partial derivatives through order two exist and are continuous ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). A coordinate partial such as $S_{c,U}$ is the ordinary derivative in that coordinate direction while every other physical coordinate is held fixed, as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

Define the **absolute thermodynamic temperature**, **entropic pressure**, and **molar chemical potential** of species $j$ by

$$T_c:=\frac{1}{S_{c,U}},\qquad p_c:=T_cS_{c,V},\qquad \mu_{c,j}:=-T_cS_{c,n_j}.$$

The entropy unit is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, the energy $U$ is in joules, $V$ is in cubic metres, and $n_j$ is in moles ([[def-td-si-quantities]]). Thus $S_{c,U}$ has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$, $T_c$ is finite and positive in kelvins, $S_{c,V}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$ and $p_c$ has units pascals, and $S_{c,n_j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ and $\mu_{c,j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$. If a microscopic model instead uses a dimensionless particle count $N_j=N_{\!A}n_j$, the corresponding per-particle chemical potential is $\mu_{c,j}/N_{\!A}$ joules, with the exact SI Avogadro constant from [[def-td-si-quantities]].

These are scalar state functions of the stated rest-frame equilibrium chart. The pressure in this definition is a derivative-defined conjugate; identifying it with force per area requires a separate adopted mechanical coupling. citations.quote:
Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq 1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$, and a bounded measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer and the physical number density corresponding to $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$, write $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above. A periodic model uses the declared periodic cell and sums its periodic-image pair interactions with each unordered pair counted once. These are distinct boundary preparations. The limits on this page are positional configurational limits and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

For a specified finite region and boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$, and the positional energy in [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. For each fixed $N$, specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to the dimensionless positional configuration measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$; adopt the law
$$P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=Z_{\Lambda,N}^{-1}e^{-\beta H_N(\omega)}\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad Z_{\Lambda,N}=\int e^{-\beta H_N}\,d\mu_{\Lambda,N},$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}<\infty$. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^{N(\omega)}e^{-\beta H_{N(\omega)}(\omega)}$ relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures; its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

Let $F_\beta$ be the finite concave canonical rate on the interior attainable-density interval from [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Extend it by $F_\beta(0)=0$, by its interior upper-semicontinuous limit at any finite upper endpoint of its effective domain, and by $-\infty$ outside the closed effective domain; retain the value $-\infty$ if the endpoint limit is $-\infty$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, define
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\beta),$$
whose existence is [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\bigl(F_\beta(\rho)+\alpha\rho\bigr),\qquad F_\beta(\rho)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\bigl(P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\bigr)$$
for every $\rho$ in the closed effective domain of $F_\beta$. These are thermodynamic limits of positional partition functions. They do not assert local-observable equivalence, a finite-volume endpoint realization, or a thin energy-shell limit.

derivations.claim: By [A1], the physical positional partition sum is $\Xi_L(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda_L,N}$. Set $\alpha=\log z$; then $z^N=e^{\alpha N}$. Translate the centered cube by $L/2$ in each coordinate to $[0,L)^d$; this preserves Lebesgue measure and every pair displacement, so the positional partition is exactly the free-cube sum of [L1]. The dimensionless energy conversion in [F1] matches its numerical $\widehat\beta$.

The conditional conclusion of [L1] gives a finite limit $P(\log z,\widehat\beta)$ for $|\Lambda_L|^{-1}\log\Xi_L$. Multiplying by $k_BT/\ell_0^d$, which is independent of $L$, converts the dimensionless reference-volume rate to pressure per physical volume.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $I$ be a nonempty, possibly infinite set of primitive system labels. Assume the declared family includes every finite separated product and every finite thermal join, and that every finite join-closed subfamily satisfies the hypotheses of [[pthm-td-contact-product-comparison]]. Also assume the explicit finite-factor representation of [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]] and the Axiom of Choice. Then there is a single dimensionless function $\widetilde S$ on all states of the declared finite-factor family that is additive under separation, extensive under every admitted positive scaling, and characterizes every equal-composition comparison:

$$ A\prec B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \widetilde S(A)\le \widetilde S(B). $$

For each simple chart, A7 also makes $\widetilde S$ concave on every convex region where the stated recombination operation is admitted. The result does not set the entropy unit to $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, determine additive constants across different reaction compositions, or establish empirical validity of the contact assumptions.

A cross-type mixing and reaction network consists of a declared set $\mathcal G$ of tagged composition types and a state set $X_\Gamma$ for each type. Each state set comes with a fixed formal composition $\nu_\Gamma$, and its states satisfy $\nu(x)=\nu_\Gamma$ as in [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]. These mathematical coefficients and their positive type weights are distinct from dimensioned material amounts. For physical channels the model additionally supplies endpoint quantity maps $U_\Gamma:X_\Gamma\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ and $n_\Gamma:X_\Gamma\to\mathbb R^r\,\mathrm{mol}$ in a declared finite species list, together with any separately tracked mechanical or external-field endpoint quantities. No identification of two distinct scaled tags is made.

For each channel $\alpha$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma'$, the model supplies sets $Z_\alpha$ of configurations, $\mathcal K_\alpha$ of protocol records, $\mathcal B_\alpha$ of outer-boundary records, and $\mathcal R_\alpha$ of transfer records, and equilibrium subsets and endpoint maps $\xi^-_\alpha:Z^-_\alpha\to X_\Gamma$, $\xi^+_\alpha:Z^+_\alpha\to X_{\Gamma'}$. A typed record is
$$P=(I,x^-,x^+,z,\kappa,b,r),$$
where $I=[t_0,t_1]$, $t_0<t_1$, is a finite time interval in seconds, $x^-\in X_\Gamma$, $x^+\in X_{\Gamma'}$, $z:I\to Z_\alpha$, $z(t_0)\in Z^-_\alpha$, $z(t_1)\in Z^+_\alpha$, $\xi^-_\alpha(z(t_0))=x^-$, $\xi^+_\alpha(z(t_1))=x^+$, $\kappa\in\mathcal K_\alpha$, $b\in\mathcal B_\alpha$, and $r\in\mathcal R_\alpha$. Transfer maps $Q_\alpha,W_{\mathrm{on},\alpha}:\mathcal R_\alpha\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ and $N_\alpha:\mathcal R_\alpha\to\mathbb R^r\,\mathrm{mol}$ record heat, work and material transfer with declared signs; any tracked $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}$ and $\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}$ are also joule-valued record maps. The channel specifies a balance predicate on this typed record set, or equivalently a balance map into a declared product of quantity spaces whose required value is zero, and a model-admitted subset satisfying that predicate. The predicate states the actual energy and material constraints of that channel; no balance law, physical admission or endpoint realizability follows from the tuple alone. For a fixed-constitution core closed channel, its endpoint embeddings, fields and admitted subset are exactly those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], with no material transfer and its stated kinetic/external restrictions. Other channels require their own adopted constraints. Define $(\Gamma,x)\mathcal R(\Gamma',y)$ exactly when an admitted channel record has those endpoints. No channel is inferred from separated composition.

For any permitted equal-formal-mass compound states $A,B$ of the network, define $A\prec B$ exactly when at least one admitted channel record has initial state $A$ and final state $B$; for named single types this is the relation $\mathcal R$ above. This is the exact relation supplied to [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], not a separate abstract order that enlarges or restricts the channel edges. Its extension to finite tagged products and common spectators is governed by the adopted A1–A6 conditions below. Thus every edge in a decorated chain is precisely an admitted channel transition. This identification is a declared model condition.

The network is **finite-factor closed** when its types admit the declared finite composition and positive scaling operations and each allowed channel respects the model’s stated conservation constraints. In addition, each channel must preserve the dimensionless formal mass $m$ of [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]]; this is the equal-coefficient-mass convention required by the mathematical chain-cost supplier, not a statement that formal mass is kilograms or moles. The common relation on all equal-formal-mass compounds satisfies A1–A6 of [[post-td-accessibility-a1-a6]], including consistency with spectators and stability. A decorated finite chain is exactly a finite sequence of such allowed transitions with a common catalyst and the real baseline-entropy edge costs in [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]].

For $\Gamma,\Gamma'$, let $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}$ be the infimum of those finite decorated-chain costs, with $+\infty$ if no witness exists and $-\infty$ if costs are unbounded below. The network has **no sinks** when, for every ordered type pair,

$$F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F(\Gamma',\Gamma)<+\infty.$$

No-sinks is an explicit property required of a network used in the global-offset theorem; it is not proved by this definition, and it is not asserted for every physical mixing or reaction. The definition permits the channel set to be empty; then the condition must still be checked rather than inferred.

Assume the calibrated entropy family of [[thm-tdmath-arbitrary-family-calibration]], the cross-type accessibility axioms A1–A6 of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], and the decorated cost $F$ of [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]. For every pair of types $\Gamma,\Gamma'$ and states $x\in X_\Gamma$, $y\in X_{\Gamma'}$,

$$x\prec y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sigma_\Gamma(x)+F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\le \sigma_{\Gamma'}(y).$$

The infimum defining $F$ need not be attained. If $F=+\infty$, the right side is false; if $F=-\infty$, the right side is true.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $F$ be the decorated cost of [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]], and assume the **no-sinks condition**

$$F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F(\Gamma',\Gamma)<+\infty$$

for every type pair. Let $V_F$ be the real difference space of [[def-tdmath-cost-offset-difference-space]]. Then there is an additive extensive offset $B:\mathcal G\to\mathbb R$ such that

$$-F(\Gamma',\Gamma)\le B(\Gamma)-B(\Gamma')\le F(\Gamma,\Gamma').$$

If every admitted cross-type transition $x\prec y$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma'$ satisfies the calibrated cost inequality of [[thm-tdmath-unattained-cost-entropy-inference]], then $\sigma_\Gamma(x)+B(\Gamma)$ is nondecreasing across every such transition. Only this weak inequality is asserted; no-gap equalities and strict extensions are not concluded.

derivations.claim: Fix an admitted transition $(\Gamma,x)\mathcal R(\Gamma',y)$. [F1] supplies finite baseline state values on both endpoint types, and [F2] identifies the decorated-chain cost convention used for this pair. Use the composition-preserving type-weighted representation from [F1]'s construction: interpret each encoded coefficient by its amount divided by the positive type weight, keeping the raw scaled and joined tags distinct. The network compares equal formal masses, and this interpretation preserves its admitted endpoint relation and each finite baseline entropy sum; hence each physical finite-chain witness and its coefficient-map image have the same real edge costs. Reversible regrouping of factors uses the adopted reversible-splitting axiom in [F2], so it changes neither the represented endpoints nor their baseline values. The cost $F$ used by [F3] is therefore this exact witness infimum, not one inferred from coordinate equality. Applying [F3] to this exact transition gives $$ \sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)-\sigma_\Gamma(x)\ge F(\Gamma,\Gamma'). $$ If the edge exists, the one-edge chain makes $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty$, so this inequality has an ordinary real right side under the stated no-sinks hypothesis.

The network’s no-sinks condition and [A1] match the hypotheses of [F4]; its cost is the same $F$ as in step 1.1 by [F2] and [F3]. Thus [F4] supplies one offset function $B$, common to all types, with additivity, positive-scale extensivity and $B(\Gamma)-B(\Gamma')\le F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$ for every pair.

Subtract the bound in step 2.1 from that in step 1.1: $$ [\sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)+B(\Gamma')]-[\sigma_\Gamma(x)+B(\Gamma)]\ge0. $$ By the definition of $S$ in the Statement, this is $S_{\Gamma'}(y)\ge S_\Gamma(x)$. The same $B$ works for every admitted transition, proving the conditional weak entropy principle.

Let $P$ be a set of primitive type labels. A formal type $\Gamma$ records a finitely supported amount function $\nu_\Gamma:P\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$, not identically zero. Primitive generators have their unit amount function. Positive scaling, separated product, and thermal-join constructors retain distinct formal tags and obey

$$\nu_{s\Gamma}=s\nu_\Gamma,\qquad \nu_{\Gamma\otimes\Gamma'}=\nu_\Gamma+\nu_{\Gamma'}\qquad(s>0).$$

Separated and joined types are distinct constructors even when their amount functions agree. Permutation, reassociation, and scaled-splitting conventions preserve the amount function. Define the positive **bookkeeping weight** $w_\Gamma:=\sum_{p\in P}\nu_\Gamma(p)$, a finite sum over support. Thus $w_{s\Gamma}=s w_\Gamma$ and every product or join has weight $w_\Gamma+w_{\Gamma'}$. The optional empty unit has zero amount function and weight zero; it is represented only by the empty compound, not as a simple chart. These are formal amounts, not masses in kilograms or an empirical conservation law. The functions and pointwise operations use [[def-function-space]]; their finite-support convention and finite sums are those of [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]] and [[lem-tdmath-compound-mass-well-defined]].

Let $I$ index the declared family of simple types $\Gamma_i$. For each simple type $\Gamma$ in that family, let $n_\Gamma\ge1$ and let $\Gamma\subset\mathbb R^{n_\Gamma+1}$ be nonempty, open and convex, with coordinates $x=(u,v)$. The notation for a type and its chart is shared, but each state has a distinct raw tag $(\Gamma,x)$. Scaled charts are distinct tagged copies $s\Gamma=\{sx:x\in\Gamma\}$ with coordinate transport $x\mapsto sx$; transported raw tags remain distinct from the original raw tags. Let $e_{(\Gamma,x)}$ be the unit point mass from [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]]. The represented state is

$$\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x):=w_\Gamma e_{(\Gamma,x)},\qquad m(\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x))=w_\Gamma.$$

Write $\mathsf{J}(x):=\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ when $x$ already carries its type tag. All state notation in this framework's compound comparisons, including a bare $x$, denotes $\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$; a raw unit point mass is always written $e_{(\Gamma,x)}$. A separated pair is addition of represented states, not a unit product tag. Nonnegative multiples are pointwise and zero terms are omitted. For an encoded compound $c$, its aggregate composition is the finite amount function

$$\nu(c):=\sum_{(\Gamma,x)\in\operatorname{supp}(c)}\frac{c(\Gamma,x)}{w_\Gamma}\nu_\Gamma;\qquad m(c)=\sum_{p\in P}\nu(c)(p).$$

Fix the formal interpretation $\Pi(c)$ as the finite separated preparation whose factor at each nonzero raw tag $(\Gamma,x)$ is the amount $c(\Gamma,x)/w_\Gamma$ of that typed state, using the declared coordinate scaling transport. The accessibility relation on coefficient maps is the pullback of the declared relation on these preparations. Merging or splitting repeated copies of the same preparation is reversible; permutation and reassociation preserve the preparation. Thus $\Pi(\mathsf{J}_{s\Gamma}(sx))$ and $\Pi(s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x))$ are the same declared scaled preparation and yield

$$\mathsf{J}_{s\Gamma}(sx)\sim s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x),$$

although their raw point masses have different tags and are not equal. This reversible transport commutes with finite composition, nested type constructors, and scaled splitting. It is part of the precise formal scaling interpretation, not a deduction about physical accessibility from coordinate multiplication. A physical use must adopt the stated preparation maps and accessibility assumptions; fixed-composition models compare only preparations with the same $\nu$, while a declared channel model may additionally compare different compositions of equal $m$.

A comparison $A\prec B$ is defined only when $m(A)=m(B)$, as in the coefficient-map supplier. Write $A\sim B$ when both directions hold, and $A\prec\prec B$ when only the forward direction holds. On any fixed simple type, dividing every represented state by the same positive constant $w_\Gamma$ gives its unit-point-mass comparison. Positive scaling and its inverse preserve and reflect order; whenever the required CH and reference hypotheses hold, the unit-state entropy theorem applies after that normalization. If $S$ represents unit-point-mass comparisons, the entropy of a represented state is $w_\Gamma S(x)$ and the entropy of a finite sum $\sum_j t_j\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x_j)$ is $\sum_j t_j w_\Gamma S(x_j)$. No independent rescaling across different types is assumed without a calibrator.

The common relation satisfies A1–A6 on all equal-mass finite compounds: (A1) reflexivity; (A2) transitivity; (A3) if $A\prec B$, then $A+C\prec B+C$ for every compound $C$; (A4) if $A\prec B$, then $tA\prec tB$ for every $t>0$; (A5) $t\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ is equivalent to $s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)+(t-s)\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ for $t>0$ and $0<s<t$, with the reversible scaled-copy transport above; (A6) for equal-mass $A,B$, fixed positive equal-mass spectators $Z_0,Z_1$, and every sequence $\epsilon_n>0$ decreasing to zero, $A+\epsilon_n Z_0\prec B+\epsilon_n Z_1$ for all $n$ implies $A\prec B$. These are hypotheses, not conclusions. No comparison hypothesis is included here.

For each $i$ and $x\in\Gamma_i$, define the forward sector $A_x:=\{y\in\Gamma_i:\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)\prec\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(y)\}$. The simple-domain assumptions are: (A7) for $x,y\in\Gamma_i$ and $0<t<1$, the encoded compound $t\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)+(1-t)\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(y)$ compares to $\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(tx+(1-t)y)$; both have bookkeeping mass $w_{\Gamma_i}$, and convexity puts the recombined coordinate in the chart; (S1) each $x$ has a strict successor; (S2) $A_x$ has exactly one supporting hyperplane at $x$, expressible as $u-u_x+P_i(x)\cdot(v-v_x)=0$ with a finite-valued slope map $P_i:\Gamma_i\to\mathbb R^{n_i}$, and $P_i$ is locally Lipschitz; (S3) the boundary of $A_x$ relative to $\Gamma_i$ is arcwise connected. A supporting hyperplane means that $A_x$ lies in one of its closed half-spaces and meets the plane at $x$. The affine hull is the smallest affine subspace containing a set; relative interior is interior in that affine hull. Closure and boundary are taken in the indicated affine hull or in $\Gamma_i$, as named; boundary is closure intersected with closure of the complement in that relative topology.

This definition imposes no physical interpretation, units, or empirical claim. A contact theorem that uses joins must separately assume that each join is a simple domain satisfying these same forward-sector hypotheses.

For two simple domains $\Gamma_i\subset\mathbb R^{n_i+1}$ and $\Gamma_j\subset\mathbb R^{n_j+1}$, write their coordinates $(u_i,v_i)$ and $(u_j,v_j)$. Their thermal-join domain is

$$\Delta_{ij}:=\{(u,v_i,v_j):\exists u_i,u_j,\ (u_i,v_i)\in\Gamma_i,\ (u_j,v_j)\in\Gamma_j,\ u=u_i+u_j\}.$$

The joined simple type is a distinct formal tag with amount function $\nu_{\Delta_{ij}}=\nu_{\Gamma_i}+\nu_{\Gamma_j}$ and weight $w_{\Delta_{ij}}=w_{\Gamma_i}+w_{\Gamma_j}$, as defined in [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]. Encode the separated pair by $\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)+\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_j}(y)$ and a joined coordinate $Z$ by $\mathsf{J}_{\Delta_{ij}}(Z)$. Their bookkeeping masses agree, and their aggregate composition functions agree. These encoded maps and their raw tags remain distinct. Positive coordinate-scaled copies use the reversible preparation transport of that definition; nested joins preserve their finite primitive amount function under reassociation and permutation. The empty type contributes the zero map.

Write $J_{ij}(x,y)$ for the join state with the summed energy coordinate and the unchanged work coordinates. A compound pair $(x,y)$ and $J_{ij}(x,y)$ have the same total energy and work coordinates but are distinct tagged objects. Define $x\sim_T y$ exactly when $\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)+\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_j}(y)$ and $\mathsf{J}_{\Delta_{ij}}(J_{ij}(x,y))$ are accessible in both directions. Nested joins use the declared reassociation and permutation identifications.

Assume every finite join is itself a simple domain satisfying [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]. The contact hypotheses are mathematical assumptions on the common relation: (T1) $(x,y)\prec J_{ij}(x,y)$; (T2) every join state has at least one reversible split into component states at its stated coordinates, and the equal-state split of any state into positive scaled copies of itself is reversible; (T3) $\sim_T$ is transitive; (T4) for every simple state $x$ there are states $x_0,x_1$ in its domain with $x_0\prec\prec x\prec\prec x_1$ and $x_0\sim_T x_1$; (T5) for every ordered pair of simple systems, every $x$ in the first and every work coordinate $v$ in the second's projection $\rho(\Gamma_j):=\{v:\exists u,(u,v)\in\Gamma_j\}$, there is a state $y$ with work coordinate $v$ and $x\sim_T y$.

For the completed calibrator branch, add (C1) **join coherence**: whenever $x\sim_T y$, the join state $J_{ij}(x,y)$ is thermally equivalent to each of $x$ and $y$ under the nested-join identifications. The coordinate sum in the definition alone does not assert C1. In later theorem statements, T1–T5 and C1 are explicitly listed as hypotheses; they are not treated as established physical laws.

Assume [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]] and T1–T4 of [[def-tdmath-thermal-contact-hypotheses]] for every finite join. For any one simple type $\Gamma_i$, every two finite compounds of its scaled copies with the same total coefficient mass are comparable. Thus CH holds on all multiple scaled products of that type. No entropy across different material types is asserted here.

Let $X$ be nonempty and suppose its finite-support compounds carry the comparison structure of [[def-tdmath-comparison-and-stability]] over the complete ordered field $\mathbb R$. If there are $x_0,x_1\in X$ with $x_0\preceq x_1$ and not $x_1\preceq x_0$, define $S(x):=\sup L_x$ using [[lem-tdmath-reference-supremum-bounds]]. Then $S:X\to\mathbb R$ is normalized by $S(x_0)=0$, $S(x_1)=1$, and for all equal-mass compounds $A=\sum_i a_i e_{x_i}$ and $B=\sum_j b_j e_{y_j}$,

$$A\preceq B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sum_i a_iS(x_i)\le\sum_j b_jS(y_j).$$

Thus $S$ is an additive extensive representation on finite compounds. If no strict pair exists, CH instead makes every equal-mass pair of compounds equivalent, and any constant state function gives a (degenerate) additive representation. No concavity, continuity, or physical law follows without additional hypotheses.

Let $\Gamma\subset\mathbb R^{n+1}$ be a simple domain satisfying the forward-sector hypotheses and T1–T4. Let $S$ be the additive extensive entropy supplied by [[thm-tdmath-additive-entropy-representation]] after CH for its finite scaled products is proved by [[thm-tdmath-reference-strip-gluing]]. Then either all pairs of states in $\Gamma$ are thermally equivalent, or there are $x,y$ on one entropy level (equivalently, one adiabat $\partial A_x$ by [[thm-tdmath-sector-nesting]]) with $x\not\sim_T y$.

Under [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], the sectors are nested: if $y\in A_x$, then $A_y\subseteq A_x$; equality holds when $y\in\partial A_x$, and $A_y\subset\operatorname{int}_{\Gamma_i}A_x$ when $y\in\operatorname{int}_{\Gamma_i}A_x$. For every $x,y\in\Gamma_i$, either $x\prec y$ or $y\prec x$ (possibly both). Strict comparison is exactly interior membership: $x\prec\prec y$ if and only if $y\in\operatorname{int}_{\Gamma_i}A_x$.

Under [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], each simple domain has one orientation sign $\varepsilon_i\in\{-1,1\}$, constant across the domain, such that at fixed work coordinate $v$, $x\prec y$ exactly when $\varepsilon_i(u_y-u_x)\ge0$. In coordinates oriented so $\varepsilon_i=1$, for each $x\in\Gamma_i$ the projection $\rho_x$ of $\partial_{\Gamma_i}A_x$ onto work coordinates is open and connected; the boundary is the graph $(u_x(v),v)$ of a $C^1$ function with locally Lipschitz derivative

$$Du_x(v)=-P_i(u_x(v),v).$$

If $y\in\partial A_x$, then $A_y=A_x$ and their boundary graphs agree.

Under A1–A6 of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], for compounds $A,B$ with $m(A)=m(B)$ and every finite spectator compound $C$, $A+C\prec B+C$ if and only if $A\prec B$. Consequently, for finite-support signed maps $u,v$ of equal total coefficient, define $u\preceq_s v$ by $(v-u)^-\prec(v-u)^+$. This relation is well-defined, agrees with $\prec$ on nonnegative maps, is invariant under adding a common signed map, is transitive, and is closed under addition of two comparisons. No comparison hypothesis is used.

Let $u,v$ be finite-support real coefficient maps on the tagged state labels of [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]] with equal total coefficient. For a typed state $x$, compound notation uses the represented map $\mathsf{J}(x)$ from [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]; its raw unit point mass is $e_{(\Gamma,x)}$. Signed maps still use the ordinary total of their raw coefficients, exactly the bookkeeping mass of the represented nonnegative maps. Put $d=v-u$, $d^+(x)=\max(d(x),0)$ and $d^-(x)=\max(-d(x),0)$. Define $u\preceq_s v$ to mean $d^-\prec d^+$ under the compound relation of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]. Write $u\sim_s v$ when both $u\preceq_s v$ and $v\preceq_s u$. These are formal signed comparison maps, not physical negative amounts. The positive and negative parts are finite-support compounds of equal mass. If $u\sim_s v$, then $cu\sim_s cv$ for every real $c$: positive $c$ uses scaling, $c=0$ is reflexivity, and negative $c$ swaps the positive and negative parts while equivalence supplies both comparison directions. This Definition introduces the signed notation; ordinary-order compatibility and the signed-order laws are proved separately.

Let a family of simple domains satisfy [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], and suppose every pair has an admitted simple thermal join satisfying T1 and T2 of [[def-tdmath-thermal-contact-hypotheses]]. Then the fixed-work orientation signs from [[thm-tdmath-forward-boundary-graph]] agree throughout the family. One common affine proof-coordinate convention $u'=\varepsilon u$, $\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, therefore makes each fixed-work accessibility order increase with $u'$ and preserves the energy-sum formula for joins. This is a mathematical coordinate convention; it does not change a physical energy quantity or assert a sign of a measured temperature.

derivations.claim: Work in [F8]'s common affine mathematical energy orientation, without redefining any physical energy or calibration. Apply [F1] and [F2] to each simple type, including every finite join, using the positive normalization by its fixed weight in [A1]. Throughout, entropy at a state means its represented-state value: $w_\Gamma$ times its unit-point-mass representation. This normalization preserves order and finite scalar amounts. The convex-combination access hypothesis in [A1] makes each resulting entropy concave, since the comparison of a scaled pair with its convex-combination state translates under the representation to the concavity inequality. By [F4], each entropy is strictly increasing with energy at fixed work coordinates.

Use T5 to choose $\bar x\in\Gamma_1$ and $\bar y\in\Gamma_2$ with $\bar x\sim_T\bar y$. Let $\phi=J_{12}(\bar x,\bar y)$ and consider its adiabat $\partial A_\phi$. T2 gives every $Z$ on that adiabat at least one split $Z=J_{12}(x_Z,y_Z)$ with $x_Z\sim_T y_Z$.

Suppose a join state $Z$ on $\partial A_\phi$ has two distinct equilibrium splits $(x^{(1)},y^{(1)})$ and $(x^{(2)},y^{(2)})$. By the definition of $\sim_T$, both pairs are reversible with $Z$, hence mutually accessible compounds. Their work coordinates are fixed by $Z$ and their total energies equal its energy. If the first-component energies agreed, both component states in the splits would agree, so distinctness forces unequal first-component energies. If $u_{x^{(1)}}<u_{x^{(2)}}$, fixed-work comparison [F4] gives $x^{(1)}\prec\prec x^{(2)}$; conservation of total energy gives $u_{y^{(2)}}<u_{y^{(1)}}$, hence $y^{(2)}\prec\prec y^{(1)}$. Taking $(x_0,x_1,y_0,y_1)=(x^{(1)},x^{(2)},y^{(2)},y^{(1)})$ gives $(x_0,y_1)\sim(x_1,y_0)$ because both split compounds are reversible with $Z$. If the first energies occur in the opposite order, swap the two splits and obtain the same calibrator form. Therefore, if no calibrator exists, every $Z\in\partial A_\phi$ has a unique equilibrium split.

Assume no calibrator exists. For any equilibrium split $(x_Z,y_Z)$ of $Z\in\partial A_\phi$, reversibility with $Z$ and the common adiabat give $(x_Z,y_Z)\sim(\bar x,\bar y)$ as compounds. By [F1], $x_Z$ and $\bar x$ are comparable; [F4] says their sectors coincide exactly when they are equivalent. If $x_Z\prec\prec\bar x$, pair reversibility gives $(\bar x,\bar y)\prec(x_Z,y_Z)$. Consistency adds $\bar y$ to $x_Z\prec\bar x$, and cancellation [F5] gives $\bar y\prec y_Z$. If $y_Z\prec\bar y$, consistency and the pair comparison instead cancel to give $\bar x\prec x_Z$, a contradiction. Thus $\bar y\prec\prec y_Z$, making a calibrator. The case $\bar x\prec\prec x_Z$ is symmetric: it gives $y_Z\prec\prec\bar y$, again a calibrator. Since neither is allowed under the assumption, $x_Z\sim\bar x$. Adding spectators to the two directions and cancelling by [F5] then gives both $\bar y\prec y_Z$ and $y_Z\prec\bar y$, so $y_Z\sim\bar y$. Thus every split on this adiabat has components in the corresponding component adiabats.

Under the no-calibrator assumption, fix a first-component work coordinate $v_1$ in the projection of $\partial A_{\bar x}$. The boundary-graph result [F4] gives exactly one state $x_*$ on that component adiabat at $v_1$. Every split of a join state on $\partial A_\phi$ with first work coordinate $v_1$ therefore has first component $x_*$. Each split is thermal, so $x_*\sim_T y_Z$ for its second component. T3 makes all such $y_Z$ thermally equivalent, and C1 makes each joined state $J(x_*,y_Z)=Z$ thermally equivalent to $x_*$. Hence all join states on this adiabat over fixed $v_1$ lie in one thermal class. Fixing a second-component work coordinate instead gives the corresponding conclusion for first components.

Let $\Omega$ be the open connected work-coordinate projection of $\partial A_\phi$ from [F4]. From any point of $\Omega$, the set reachable by finitely many coordinate-axis segments contained in open boxes in $\Omega$ is relatively open, and its complement is also relatively open; connectedness makes the reachable set all of $\Omega$. Along each such segment, step 4.1 gives equivalence of the corresponding join states; T3 composes these finitely many equivalences. Thus the whole adiabat $\partial A_\phi$ is one thermal class. Since the argument works for every starting join state, every join adiabat is one thermal class.

Still assuming no calibrator, apply [F3] to each join system. Its alternative with two thermally inequivalent states on one adiabat is excluded by step 5.1, so all states of each join system are thermally equivalent. For any $x,x'\in\Gamma_1$, use T5 with one allowed second work coordinate to choose $y,y'$ with $x\sim_T y$ and $x'\sim_T y'$. C1 relates each component to its joined state, and all join states are in one thermal class; T3 therefore gives $x\sim_T x'$. The same argument gives one thermal class in $\Gamma_2$. Now take $Z=\phi\in\partial A_\phi$ and a split $(x,y)$ supplied by T2. Choose nonzero sufficiently small $\delta$ so $(u_x+\delta,v_1)\in\Gamma_1$ and $(u_y-\delta,v_2)\in\Gamma_2$, possible because the domains are open. These states form a distinct split of the same $Z$. Since the original split has $x\sim_T y$ and each component type is one thermal class, T3 gives thermal equivalence of the changed pair as well. This contradicts uniqueness of the split from step 2.1. Therefore a calibrator exists.

Fix a calibrator $x_0\prec\prec x_1$, $y_0\prec\prec y_1$, whose existence is step 6.1. Choose same-type entropy representatives $S_1,S_2$ from [F2], with positive gaps $h_1=S_1(x_1)-S_1(x_0)$ and $h_2=S_2(y_1)-S_2(y_0)$. Normalize $\widetilde S_i=S_i/h_i$, so both calibrator increments are one, and put $s(x)=\widetilde S_1(x)-\widetilde S_1(x_0)$ and $t(y)=\widetilde S_2(y)-\widetilde S_2(y_0)$. Write $u=\mathsf{J}(x_0)+\mathsf{J}(y_1)$ and $v=\mathsf{J}(x_1)+\mathsf{J}(y_0)$. The calibrator says $u\sim v$, so $v-u=(\mathsf{J}(x_1)-\mathsf{J}(x_0))-(\mathsf{J}(y_1)-\mathsf{J}(y_0))$ is equivalent to zero; translation and cancellation [F5] give $(\mathsf{J}(x_1)-\mathsf{J}(x_0))\sim_s(\mathsf{J}(y_1)-\mathsf{J}(y_0))$. For any state $x$, the signed map $d_x=\mathsf{J}(x)-(1-s(x))\mathsf{J}(x_0)-s(x)\mathsf{J}(x_1)$ has total mass and $\widetilde S_1$-value zero. Its positive and negative parts have equal mass and entropy, so [F2] makes them equivalent. Hence $\mathsf{J}(x)\sim_s(1-s(x))\mathsf{J}(x_0)+s(x)\mathsf{J}(x_1)$; the same argument applies to states of the second type. These are formal signed maps when a coefficient lies outside $[0,1]$.

For a state pair $(x,y)$, put $\lambda=(s(x)+t(y))/2$ and $\delta=(s(x)-t(y))/2$. Adding the signed reductions from step 7.1 makes the pair equivalent to $(1-\lambda)(\mathsf{J}(x_0)+\mathsf{J}(y_0))+\lambda(\mathsf{J}(x_1)+\mathsf{J}(y_1))$ plus $\delta[(\mathsf{J}(x_1)-\mathsf{J}(x_0))-(\mathsf{J}(y_1)-\mathsf{J}(y_0))]$. The calibrator increment equivalence from step 7.1 makes the latter term equivalent to zero for either sign of $\delta$. Thus each pair reduces to its reference map at parameter $\lambda$. For any finite compound $A$ with amounts $M_1,M_2$ of the two types, add and scale these single-state reductions. Writing $q_1(A),q_2(A)$ for the amount-weighted sums of $s(x),t(y)$, respectively, gives $A\sim_s(M_1-q_1(A))\mathsf{J}(x_0)+q_1(A)\mathsf{J}(x_1)+(M_2-q_2(A))\mathsf{J}(y_0)+q_2(A)\mathsf{J}(y_1)$. Using $(\mathsf{J}(x_1)-\mathsf{J}(x_0))\sim_s(\mathsf{J}(y_1)-\mathsf{J}(y_0))$, this is equivalent to $M_1\mathsf{J}(x_0)+M_2\mathsf{J}(y_0)+Q(A)(\mathsf{J}(x_1)-\mathsf{J}(x_0))$, where $Q(A)=q_1(A)+q_2(A)$. If the total mass is zero, both compounds are empty and reflexivity compares them. Otherwise, for same-composition $A,B$, their base terms agree. If $Q(A)<Q(B)$, the positive and negative parts of the reference-map difference are $(Q(B)-Q(A))\mathsf{J}(x_1)$ and $(Q(B)-Q(A))\mathsf{J}(x_0)$, so $x_0\prec x_1$ and positive scaling compares the maps forward. If the Q values agree the maps coincide; if $Q(A)>Q(B)$ the reverse comparison holds. Translation, addition, and ordinary-order compatibility [F5] transfer the result to $A,B$. This proves CH for every fixed finite composition of the two types and their scaled copies.

Let $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ be simple domains in a family of finite thermal joins satisfying A1–A7, S1–S3, T1–T5, and C1 of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]] and [[def-tdmath-thermal-contact-hypotheses]]. Then there are $x_0\prec\prec x_1$ in $\Gamma_1$ and $y_0\prec\prec y_1$ in $\Gamma_2$ such that

$$(x_0,y_1)\sim(x_1,y_0).$$

Moreover, for every fixed finite composition of scaled copies of $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$, any two equal-mass states of that same composition are comparable (CH). The conclusion is conditional on the explicitly stated join-coherence and universal-range assumptions C1 and T5.

citations.quote: Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB.

The normalized unit-intensity Poisson version is $Z_Q(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,\mathrm{free}}}]$; since the Poisson density contributes $e^{-V_L}$, $\Xi(L;z,\beta)=e^{V_L}Z_Q(L;z,\beta)$.

For the unit cells $C_i=i+[0,1)^d$, there are constants $A>0$ and $B\geq0$ such that every finite configuration satisfies
$$H_\phi(\omega)\geq A\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}N_{C_i}(\omega)^2-BN(\omega).$$
Only finitely many summands are nonzero.
Then $\mathcal H_c$ is compact and sequentially compact in $\tau_L$.

Let $d\geq1$, let $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega)$, with this class defined in [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]], be ergodic under the full translation group $\mathbb R^d$, and suppose its specific relative entropy $I(P)=\gamma$ relative to the unit-intensity Poisson law $Q$ is finite.
A real measurable function $f$ on $\Omega$ is local if there is a bounded Borel set $A$ such that $f$ is measurable with respect to the restriction $\omega\mapsto\omega|_A$.
Let $\phi$ be stable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], with stability constant $B$, and fix $a,\beta>0$.

Let $0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$ be measurable and suppose $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$
for every $x$.

Assume AC. Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on one measurable space and use $D(P\Vert Q)$ as defined in [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Then
$$D(P\Vert Q)=\sup_{\phi\in B_b}\left(P(\phi)-\log Q(e^\phi)\right),$$
where $B_b$ is the set of bounded real measurable functions. In particular $D\geq0$. If $T$ is measurable, then $D(P\circ T^{-1}\Vert Q\circ T^{-1})\leq D(P\Vert Q)$.

For standard-Borel spaces $X,Y$, probability reference measures $Q_X,Q_Y$, and a joint probability $P_{XY}\ll Q_X\otimes Q_Y$ with finite $D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)$, let $P_{Y|X=x}$ be the conditional law supplied by [[thm-conditional-density-formula]]. Then
$$D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)=D(P_X\Vert Q_X)+\int_X D(P_{Y|X=x}\Vert Q_Y)\,P_X(dx).$$
More generally, for random variables $R,S,Y$ taking values in standard-Borel spaces $\mathcal R,\mathcal S,\mathcal Y$, with $R=r(S)$ for a measurable $r:\mathcal S\to\mathcal R$, and a probability reference $Q_Y$ on $\mathcal Y$, the conditional increments
$$G(R):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|R}\Vert Q_Y)\right],\qquad G(S):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|S}\Vert Q_Y)\right]$$
satisfy $0\leq G(R)\leq G(S)$ whenever $D(P_{S,Y}\Vert P_S\otimes Q_Y)<\infty$.

If $P$ and $Q$ are probability measures on the same measurable space, define
$$D(P\Vert Q)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\int h\log h\,dQ,&P\ll Q\text{ and }h=dP/dQ,\\+\infty,&P\not\ll Q.\end{cases}$$
Use $0\log0=0$.

derivations.claim: Georgii's Theorem 1 [L1] gives existence of $\Phi(P)$ and lower semicontinuity for every stationary finite-intensity law. Its Euclidean radial tail hypothesis follows from ours: $|x|_\infty\leq|x|_2\leq\sqrt d\,|x|_\infty$, so replacing $\psi(r)$ by $\psi(r/\sqrt d)$ preserves monotonicity and finite weighted integral by a change of variables. The stable-plus-positive-core definition matches the source's superstable condition after choosing a smaller Euclidean core ball. Thus $\Phi$ has exactly the domain and convention in the Statement.

The cell estimate [F2] and $\beta>0$ imply $J=I+\beta\Phi-\rho\log z$ is lower semicontinuous and coercive on bounded-$J$ sets: the Poisson entropy variational inequality with bounded truncations of $aN_{C_0}$ gives $I(P)\geq a\rho(P)-(e^a-1)$; the pointwise square inequality gives $E_PN_{C_0}^2\geq\rho(P)^2$. Hence bounded $J$ bounds $\rho$, $I$, and $\Phi$ from above. A finite candidate exists: take independent Bernoulli occupancy of widely separated small cubes, at most one absolutely continuously distributed point per cube, and a uniform random lattice phase. Each tile has finite relative entropy to Poisson, and the summable regular tail bounds its absolute intertile energy per volume. Thus $J$ is proper. By [F3] and the choice assumptions [A1], its bounded sublevels are compact in $\tau_L$.

For the finite-volume Gibbs tilt $G_{L,z,\beta,bc}$, direct integration gives $$ L^{-d}\log Z_{L,z,\beta,bc} =-L^{-d}D(G_{L,z,\beta,bc}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_L}) -\beta L^{-d}E_GH_{L,bc} +L^{-d}\log z\,E_GN. $$ Georgii's Theorem 2 [L2], applied with the present superstable regular interaction and $F=0$, supplies the matching upper and lower empirical-field bounds and the free/periodic pressure limit. Its upper proof uses this entropy identity, block stationarization, and the superstable cell cutoff; its lower proof conditions finite blocks on bounded finite-energy events, inserts empty corridors, and applies the spatial likelihood limit. The inspected source hypotheses match [F1]–[F8]: the Poisson reference is independent unit intensity, $\tau_L$ is the local-tame topology [F5], entropy compactness is [F3], and the energy-density interface is [L1]. The theorem therefore yields $$ p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_P\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\} $$ for both boundary conditions, with compact variational sublevels.

The minimum is attained: a minimizing sequence lies in a finite sublevel by the sparse finite candidate in step 1.2; compactness [F3] gives a convergent subsequence and lower semicontinuity from step 1.1 gives a minimizer. The set of minimizers is the closed minimum level within that compact sublevel, hence nonempty and compact. This agrees with the compact-sublevel conclusion in [L2].

The unit-intensity Poisson law on $\Lambda_L$ has density $e^{-L^d}/N!$ relative to Lebesgue measure on the $N$-point sector. Therefore the physical partition $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}=e^{L^d}Z_{L,z,\beta,\mathrm{free}}$; its log rate is $p_Q+1$. This is only a positional normalization conversion.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and fix $z,\beta>0$. For stationary finite-intensity configuration laws, let $I(P)$ be relative entropy density with respect to the independent unit-intensity Poisson law, $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$, and $\Phi(P)$ the limiting positional energy density. The existence and lower semicontinuity of $\Phi$ under these hypotheses are part of the proof below. For free and periodic cubes define
$$Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,bc}}\right],\qquad bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$
Then the limit $p_Q(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}$ exists, is independent of $bc$, and
$$p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology $\tau_L$. This theorem concerns positional configurations only. If $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}$ is instead normalized against Lebesgue measure with $1/N!$, then $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}=e^{L^d}Z_{L,z,\beta,\mathrm{free}}$, so its logarithmic rate is $p_Q+1$.

$$p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$

For sequences $L_j\to\infty$ and integers $N_j\geq0$ with $N_j/L_j^d\to\rho$, define
$$b(\rho)=\sup\left\{\limsup_{j\to\infty}L_j^{-d}\log Z(L_j,N_j;\beta):\frac{N_j}{L_j^d}\to\rho\right\}.$$
Let $F$ be the concave envelope of $b$ on $[0,\infty)$, namely the supremum of $\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i b(\rho_i)$ over finite lists with $\theta_i\geq0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, $\rho_i\geq0$, and $\sum_i\theta_i\rho_i=\rho$; the empty supremum is $-\infty$.

For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, define
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\beta),$$
whose existence is [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]].

For free and periodic cubes define
$$Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,bc}}\right],\qquad bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$
Then the limit $p_Q(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}$ exists, is independent of $bc$, and
$$p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology $\tau_L$.
For a finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, let $\omega^{(L)}=\{q+Lk:q\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ be its periodic continuation.

For $L>0$ and a finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ with $N(\omega)=N$, the measure $R_{L,\omega}$ of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]] is a stationary probability law of finite intensity and
$$\rho(R_{L,\omega})=\frac{N}{L^d}.$$
For any probability law $C_L$ on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L$ with $E_{C_L}N<\infty$, its empirical-field barycenter $\bar C_L$ is also a stationary probability law of finite intensity and $\rho(\bar C_L)=E_{C_L}N/L^d$.

Let $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $\beta,z>0$, and $b\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}$. On the simple labelled sector $\mathcal S_{L,N}=\{q\in\Lambda_L^N:q_i\neq q_j\ (i\neq j)\}$ use $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}(q)=\sum_{i<j}\phi(q_i-q_j)$ and the periodic energy $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ from [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For $N\geq1$ define
$$Z_b(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\mathcal S_{L,N}}e^{-\beta H_{L,b}(q)}\,dq_1\cdots dq_N,\qquad Z_b(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
with $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$, and put $\Xi_b(L,z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_b(L,N;\beta)$. The unit-intensity Poisson reference $Q_{\Lambda_L}$ has sector density $e^{-L^d}/N!$ relative to labelled Lebesgue measure, so its normalized grand partition is
$$Z_{Q,b}(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,b}}]=e^{-L^d}\Xi_b(L,z,\beta).$$
The exact-$N$ canonical law $C^b_{L,N}$ has density $e^{-\beta H_{L,b}}/(N!Z_b(L,N;\beta))$ on $\mathcal S_{L,N}$, and the grand-canonical law $G^b_{L,z,\beta}$ has density $z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,b}}/Z_{Q,b}(L;z,\beta)$ relative to $Q_{\Lambda_L}$. Let $\rho>0$ be an interior attainable density, choose $\alpha=\log z$ supporting the free canonical rate $F_\beta$ at $\rho$, and take $N_L/L^d\to\rho$. Assume
$$L^{-d}\log Z_b(L,N_L;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho).$$
Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]], and let
$$\mathcal M_{z,\beta}:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
Then for every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood $U$ of $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}$ there is $c_U>0$ such that
$$\limsup_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log C^b_{L,N_L}\{\,\omega:R_{L,\omega}\notin U\,\}\leq-c_U.$$
If $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}=\{P_*\}$, then $R_{L,\omega}\to P_*$ in probability in $\tau_L$ under $C^b_{L,N_L}$. This is a statement about spatially averaged local observables through the empirical field, not about the raw finite-box law at a fixed origin.

derivations.claim: Since $\rho$ is interior and $F_\beta$ is finite and concave there by [F1], it has a finite supporting slope $\alpha$ at $\rho$. Put $z=e^\alpha>0$.

The free exact-$N$ rate hypothesis of [F5] is exactly [F1], and [F2] supplies its supporting activity. The normalized/physical pressure conversion in [F3] is the equality required by [F5]; the empirical field is the stationary one in [F4]. Applying [F5] with free boundary gives concentration on $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}$ in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood.

If the minimizer set is the singleton $\{P_*\}$, every open neighborhood of $P_*$ is a neighborhood of the full set. Step 2.1 therefore gives $C_{L,N_L}(R_{L,\omega}\notin U)\to0$ for every open $U\ni P_*$, which is convergence in probability in $\tau_L$.

Assume the superstable regular model of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], $\beta>0$, and an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. Let $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, let $C_{L,N_L}$ be the free-boundary positional canonical law with exactly $N_L$ particles, and let $R_{L,\omega}$ be its periodized empirical field from [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. Choose any finite supporting activity $z>0$ of $F_\beta$ at $\rho$ and set
$$\mathcal M_{z,\beta}:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
For every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood $U$ of $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}$,
$$C_{L,N_L}\{\omega:R_{L,\omega}\in U\}\longrightarrow1.$$
If $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}=\{P_*\}$, then $R_{L,\omega}\to P_*$ in probability in $\tau_L$. This is local observable equivalence for a uniformly sampled bulk location; it makes no claim about the raw finite-box law at a fixed origin or about uniqueness for every interaction.
